name: Method / Procedure
purpose: Represent reusable authored methods and procedures, immutable editions, applicability and adopter-owned adoption records without treating publication or adoption as execution.

owns: procedure identity and ordered instruction content
immutable released editions and errata lineage
adopter-owned adoption records and effective dates
delegates: operational process definitions and execution to WM-ACT-003
competence and credential identity to their external masters
standard identity and legal effect to external authorities
excludes: process instances work items or execution outcomes

constraints: a procedure may serve multiple methods without duplicating instruction identity
normative content is published only through an Edition manifest
contentDigest covers the complete published manifest including procedure steps
method-edition manifest transitively pins incorporated procedure edition ids and digests
effective status requires in-scope authorityRef and attestationRef
effectiveFrom before recordedAt requires separately authorized backdating
at most one effective adoption per adopter, subject and instant unless a deterministic precedence record exists
local constraints are digested narrowing only and cannot alter edition content
method manifests pin incorporated procedure edition ids and digests
procedure manifests pin all ProcedureStep keys and digests

relations.purpose: Navigate to operational definitions while the authoritative definition-to-edition binding remains process-owned.
Reference adopting or authoring organization identity without remastering it.

operations.effect: Issue an immutable edition or erratum with digest and lineage.
Issue a successor while preserving the predecessor.
Create an adopter-owned record with an effective date and authority.
End local applicability without altering the published edition.

invariants: A released edition is immutable and content-addressed.
A normative correction creates an erratum or successor edition and never edits released text in place.
Edition supersession lineage is acyclic.
Publication does not imply adoption.
Adoption takes effect on the adopter-recorded effective interval rather than publication date.
An AdoptionRecord pins exactly one edition id and digest.
The author owns released editions; the adopter owns its AdoptionRecord.
Every effective adoption has an authority and attestation reference.
Competence requirements and scope-of-use are edition-qualified.
A procedure is instruction knowledge and never records work performance.
A method states approach and rationale while a procedure states ordered instructions.
Process definitions reference adopted editions without copying their text.
Publishing a new edition never silently re-points an active or completed process.
Standard and competence references do not transfer external mastership.
Wildcard imports do not constitute standards conformance.
Publication is refused while fixturesExecuted is false, publishableCanonical is false or any release hold is open.
No two editions share one subject and version or one subject and content digest.
Every edition declares subjectKind method or procedure.
Procedure instructions and steps are edition-scoped and covered by the edition digest.
A method edition transitively pins every incorporated procedure edition id and digest.
Withdrawn editions remain permanently digest-resolvable for historical traces.
At most one adoption is effective for one adopter, subject and instant unless explicit deterministic precedence exists.
Backdated adoption requires scoped authority and never overrides immutable trace pins.
Local constraints are content-addressed narrowing only.
Legacy assembly identifiers can never label a successor candidate version.
holds: The single frozen semantic audit and its one-pass remediation are pending.
CRUD, roles, artifacts and executable package conversion are absent.
Relations are candidate-only until ledger approval.
External notation and standards crosswalks are alignments rather than conformance claims.
Registry composition_role, default_link_type and relations_ref require explicit reconciliation before release.

digestPolicy.canonicalization: RFC8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme for candidate records
digestPolicy.digestDomain: normative object content excluding local display labels and record identifiers explicitly named outside each digest

alignmentPolicy: Only a source with an exact version or digest may appear; every entry must state claim=alignment-only. No current pinned alignment is claimed.

registryActions: Bind legacy assembly id permanently to 0.2.0-legacy
Record K3/K6 spec-path rename without editing legacy bytes

referencePolicy: Every *Ref field resolves through referenceTypes; external-unmastered references must carry namespace, source and resolution rule.

referenceTypes.authorityRef: adopting organization or scoped delegation record

projections.authority: derived for adopter+subject+instant with explicit precedence

tombstonePolicy: Retraction or protected referent erasure preserves edition/adoption identity and digest-resolvable historical references.

authorityRules.adoption: authority belongs to the adopting organization or its explicit delegation
authorityRules.backdating: separate delegation required and trace pins remain authoritative
